\r
The framework will be split into four Lots as detailed below:\r

Lot 1 	Street Name Plates	Supply Only\r

Lot 3	Road Signage (including Directional Signs, Information signs)	Supply Only\r

\r
The Councils intents to award only one supplier to each Lot, however, tenderers can bid for one or more Lots; though each Lot will be evaluated separately and response documents must be provided for each lot that the tenderer is responding to. Therefore, the potential successful tenderer could be appointed to more than one lot.\r

title: HDC202410- Quotation for Hart Countryside Services Visitor Surveys - 2024
description:
Lot 1 The Council is seeking a skilled consultant to independently evaluate 5 of its key countryside sites from a visitor's perspective: 
The report will be led by the community through visitor surveys and engagement with the aim of improving the visitor experience. The report will be underpinned by spatial data. It will quantify, segment, and engage current and potential site users. It will evaluate user satisfaction providing clear guidance and advise on how the countryside service can work to enhance these sites in a meaningful way for residents. The report will suggest steps to show how these goals can be achieved and how these changes can be measured to show success.
Lot 2 Hart Countryside Services Accessibility Audit  
 The report should be set in a local context and draw on population and demographic statistics to make it specifically relevant to Hart. The report should make recommendations on how to make the sites more inclusive and appealing to underrepresented groups including those with hidden and physical disabilities. The report should reference different cultural groups in the area and consider barriers to inclusion for these groups making suggestion as to how these barriers could be overcome.

title: Advert for an Architect
description:
Hook Parish Council invites expressions of interest from Registered and /or Chartered  Architects, who have appropriate RIBA qualifications and live within 25 mile radius of the site RG27 9EQ , to act as Lead Consultant on an exciting new-build project in Hook, Hampshire .

The Project 
The provision of a new multi-purpose pavilion with independent changing facilities for the playing fields on a site north east of Hook. Also,  the provision of another new building that will be joined to the pavilion and required to accommodate workshops, material store and other facilities required by the Hook Shed. The combined buildings will have some shared facilities such as toilets and as an initial guide the floor area of the pavilion part is proposed to be approx. 450 m2 and the floor area of the Hook Shed part is proposed to be approx. 130 m2.
The Council requires a contemporary design for the pavilion and associated facilities which satisfies the planning and technical guidelines set out by the RFA and Sports Council England. The combined buildings must be sympathetic to their setting and address both the sporting activities proposed for the adjoining playing fields and the activities associated with a general-purpose workshop that is operated by volunteers.

The Role
To take the concept information provided as part of an outline brief and work-up a final layout and detailed design for the combined buildings and associated infrastructure that is suitable for a full planning application to the Local Planning Authority (Hart DC). These designs will include layout plans and construction details for all building and infrastructure works over the whole of the defined site including vehicular and pedestrian access, car parking, amenity areas and servicing of the facilities.
When developing the final layouts and the detailed designs the Architect will be required to work closely with both the Sports Working Group of the Parish Council in regard to the sports and recreational facilities associated with the pavilion and the Trustees of the Hook Shed in regard to their facilities which will provide for workshops and social activities. 
Following planning approval the Architect will be required to prepare the necessary contract documents, including all drawings, specification and supporting documents to enable the Parish Council to invite tenders for the construction of the whole of these combined facilities using an appropriate Form of Contract. 

Applications 
Submissions to be made in writing to The Parish Clerk, Hook Parish Council, Hook, Community Centre. Ravenscroft, Hook, Hampshire, RG27 9NN or by e-mail to clerk@hook.gov.uk. To include Inter-alia,  your qualifications, examples of relevant experience and at least three references. To be submitted no later than noon on 13th August 2021.

title: Locally Enhanced Services for Thurrock Alliance (NHS Mid and South Essex ICB)
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Authority, South East Essex Alliance on behalf of NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs). This Contract Award is made by the Authority to the 27 General Practitioner (GP) providers within the south east Essex (previously Castle Point and Rochford and Southend areas) geographical footprint for the provision of Locally Enhanced Services (LES).

The provision of Locally Enhanced Services to include:
- 24 Hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring
- Gonadorelin Analogue Injections
- Minor Injury Services
- Phlebotomy
- Secondary & Community Care Wound Management Services
- Non Scalpel Vasectomy Service (NSV)
- 24 Hour Electrocardiogram
- Shared Care
- Anticoagulation (Warfarin)

The Authority has taken the decision to award this Locally Enhanced Service (which was previously commissioned for NHS Castle Point and Rochford CCG and Southend CCG) to the 47incumbent General Practitioner (GP) providers. As of July 2022, the Integrated Care Board (ICB) superseded the previous 5 CCGs within Mid and South Essex. NHS Mid and South Essex ICB is currently undergoing an organisational restructure and have taken the decision to extend the current contract to the incumbent providers for 12 months whilst commissioning decisions and strategies can be made for the future of this service. The Authority considers these 47 GP providers for this LES as technically capable of providing the most economically advantageous solution to the Authority whilst the ICB undergoes restructure, review and alignment of contracts. The Authority is applying the NHS Standard Contract Terms and Conditions to ensure appropriate clinical governance and service delivery quality as well as consistency of service to patients. 

The contract will be for 12 months, from 01st April 2023 - 31st March 2024 . The aggregate contract value across the 47 General Practitioners service providers is forecasted at £468,950.00

The Authority is publishing this Contract Award Notice in the Contracts Finder in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended by The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020) for spend above £30,000.
